entry.title: String Amplitudes on Integer Rectangles
entry.summary: Hidden zeros of tree-level string amplitudes of colored scalars lie on loci specified by integer-valued dimensionless momentum contractions arranged in rectangles on the kinematic mesh. We study the same kinematic loci for open-string amplitudes with gluons, fermions and higher-spin states at arbitrary finite mass levels. Disk monodromy relations yield $\textit{zero-locus factorization}$: at regular points where the monodromy system is invertible, the amplitude is a weighted sum of physical three-point amplitudes sewn to complete on-shell $(n-1)$-point amplitudes. Hidden zeros follow when the external wavefunctions annihilate all contributing three-point couplings. In the low-energy limit, the massless zero-integer branch recovers the corresponding field-theory factorization. For closed strings, including gravitons, persistent cubic zeros in both chiral sectors remove the disk poles, allowing the Kawai--Lewellen--Tye momentum-kernel zero to imply amplitude zeros. The operator product expansions of external vertices give a common worldsheet origin for these conditions across spins and mass levels.

entry.title: Spin-resolved microscopy of $^{87}$Sr SU($N$) Fermi-Hubbard systems
entry.summary: Quantum-gas microscopes provide direct access to the phases of the Hubbard model, bringing microscopic insight into the complex competition between interactions, SU(2) magnetism, and doping. Alkaline-earth(-like) fermions extend this spin-1/2 paradigm by realizing higher symmetries and giving access to SU($N$) Hubbard models, with rich phase diagrams to be unveiled. Despite its fundamental interest, a microscopic exploration of SU($N$) quantum systems has remained elusive. Here we report the realization of a quantum-gas microscope for fermionic $^{87}$Sr. Our imaging scheme, based on cooling and fluorescence on the narrow intercombination line at 689 nm, enables spin-resolved single-atom detection. By implementing a spin-selective optical pumping protocol, we determine the occupation of each of the 10 spin states in a single experimental realization, a crucial capability for probing site-resolved magnetic correlations. We benchmark our method by observing single-particle Larmor precession across the full spin-9/2 ground-state manifold and use numerical simulations of SU($N$) Fermi-Hubbard chains, incorporating the measured detection fidelities, to demonstrate its capability to resolve many-body spin correlations. Our results establish $^{87}$Sr quantum-gas microscopy as a powerful approach to study exotic magnetism in the SU($N$) Fermi-Hubbard model, and provide a new detection tool for studies in quantum simulation, computation, and metrology.

entry.title: Timelike Supersymmetric Geometries in Seven-Dimensional Supergravity
entry.summary: Seven-dimensional supergravity poses a uniquely intricate supersymmetry problem, combining topologically massive higher-form gauge dynamics, distinct Clifford algebra properties, and rich geometric structures. We first establish the complete formulation of the maximal Cartan-gauged theory in terms of the gauge-invariant higher-form flux, including both the bosonic action and supersymmetry variations. This formulation, which also makes the smooth ungauged limit manifest, is achieved by requiring a consistent truncation to the minimal Cartan-gauged theory in the equal-charge limit. We construct the complete bilinear system for a timelike Killing vector, where additional internal orientation of the symplectic-Majorana spinor arises already in the scalar sector, uniquely among pure minimal ungauged theories. In the equal-charge sector, we decouple the algebraic constraints into SU$(3)$-isotypic components, and analyse the differential bilinear relations, determining the permitted dilaton gradient, fluxes, fibration twist and intrinsic torsion of the base. We prove that with gauging and active Cartan flux, the complex scalar bilinear vanishes identically. We also construct a Killing gauge for the higher-form potential compatible with the self-duality condition. We show that with gauging but no active Cartan flux, the Killing vector also acts as a generator of the gauged R-symmetry, and the base structure is enlarged from SU$(3)$ to U$(3)$. We find that BPS-flow solutions realize this setting. With supersymmetry, we isolate a single independent component of the 3-form equation across an exhaustive four-class partition for both theories within this setup. Applied to known and proposed solutions in both theories, this classification exposes unexplored sectors and provides an accessible toolbox for constructing and testing solutions and developing new geometric and holographic applications.

entry.title: Holographic surface defect RG flows without supersymmetry
entry.summary: We consider $\mathcal{N}=4$ supersymmetric Yang--Mills theory with gauge group SU$(N)$, which admits families of conformal surface defects defined by singular boundary conditions for scalar fields that completely break supersymmetry. At large $N$ and strong coupling, these defects are holographically dual either to a probe D5-brane or to one of two new D7-brane embeddings that we introduce in this work. We also construct embeddings of both D5- and D7-branes describing defect renormalisation group (RG) flows, for which the ultraviolet and infrared fixed points are both dual to the same D$p$-brane, with different values of a parameter. Our embeddings dual to RG flows are mostly constructed numerically, but we find a regime in which we can derive approximate analytic embeddings using a controlled perturbative expansion. We demonstrate that the $b$-theorem is satisfied by all of the RG flows that we study.

entry.title: Realization of a Superleak in a Quantum Gas
entry.summary: Ultracold quantum gases offer a controllable and microscopically accessible platform for understanding and engineering superfluidity. Yet, realizing a superleak that selectively transports the superfluid while suppressing normal flow has remained elusive. Here, we harness an optical superlattice to realize such a superleak through dynamical selectivity. The superfluid undergoes coherent Josephson transport, whereas the normal component exhibits slow, thermodynamically limited response, resulting in a flow-rate contrast of 500(49). Exploiting this contrast, we demonstrate repeated filtering of the normal component and dynamical purification of the superfluid, while sustaining coherent driven oscillations for up to 100 cycles. Our results establish a controllable atomic superleak and open possibilities for manipulating transport and thermodynamics in quantum fluids.

entry.title: The XMM-Newton view of the DEM L36 superbubble in the Large Magellanic Cloud
entry.summary: We present the first multi-wavelength analysis of the DEM L36 superbubble in the Large Magellanic Cloud. We compare the DEM L36 superbubble with other Galactic and Magellanic Cloud superbubbles. We use data from XMM-Newton, supplemented by data from the Magellanic Cloud Emission Line Survey, the Dark Energy Camera Magellanic Cloud Emission Line Survey, the Spitzer Space Telescope, and the Australia Telescope Compact Array. We perform a multi-wavelength morphological analysis to understand the shape and structure of the superbubble and X-ray spectral analysis to derive physical parameters of the hot gas. We find significant X-ray emission in DEM L36, dominated by a central bubble region mostly confined by a thin H$α$ filamentary shell. This has two distinct blowout regions to the east and west, with a possible smaller blowout in the south. Spectral analysis shows the X-ray emission is well fit with a thermal plasma model in collisional ionisation equilibrium with a temperature of $kT=0.17~(0.16-0.18)$ keV and unabsorbed luminosity $L_{X~(0.5-7.0~\mathrm{keV})}=3.62\times 10^{35} $erg s$^{-1}$. Unlike other LMC superbubbles, we find no clear powering cluster at the centre, though relatively small clusters near the edge are likely supplying the mechanical input at the present epoch. We use photometric data of these clusters to estimate cluster masses, ages, and mechanical inputs to compare with the energy stored in the superbubble. We find that these clusters have supplied more energy over their lifetime than is currently observed in the superbubble, indicative of the so-called growth rate discrepancy problem. It is likely the DEM L36 superbubble was initially shaped by a central massive stellar population that has since dispersed and largely lost to supernovae, with smaller clusters at the edges of the swept-up shell being currently supplying the energy input.

entry.title: A cosmological intercept tension in local distance ladders
entry.summary: The Hubble tension motivates direct tests of the internal consistency of the local distance ladder. We perform forward and backward consistency checks between Type Ia supernovae in Cepheid host galaxies and the Hubble-flow supernova sample using Pantheon+ data. Within flat $Λ$CDM, we impose Planck-CMB priors on one sample, infer the supernova absolute-magnitude calibration, and propagate it to the other sample to recover the Hubble constant, which should match the input value if the second and third rungs of the distance ladder align perfectly. We examine the impact of host-galaxy peculiar velocities using redshift corrections based on the Manticore-Local reconstruction. These corrections shift the recovered $H_0$ from $74.30^{+1.18}_{-1.20}$ to $71.37^{+1.23}_{-1.18}$ $\mathrm{km\,s^{-1}Mpc^{-1}}$ in the forward analysis and from $60.83^{+0.98}_{-0.97}$ to $63.25^{+0.95}_{-0.93}$ $\mathrm{km\,s^{-1}Mpc^{-1}}$ in the backward analysis, bringing both results closer to the input CMB constraint. Comparing the cosmological intercepts of the magnitude-redshift relation inferred from two rungs of the distance ladder before and after peculiar-velocity corrections, we find that the significance of the discrepancy decreases from $6.8σ$ to $3.9σ$ in the forward check and from $7.3σ$ to $4.3σ$ in the backward check. Peculiar-velocity corrections therefore partially alleviate the intercept tension, while a residual discrepancy persists within the adopted framework. Our results highlight the importance of local velocity modeling and motivate further tests of sample selection and calibration systematics in assessing distance-ladder consistency.

entry.title: Gravitational waves from highly charged binary black holes in Einstein-Maxwell-dilaton theory
entry.summary: We perform fully nonlinear numerical-relativity simulations of electrically charged binary black hole mergers in Einstein-Maxwell-dilaton (EMD) theory, varying the magnitude and relative sign of the input charges and the dilaton coupling $a$. In the weak-charge sequence, the dominant gravitational waveforms remain close to the neutral vacuum baseline of general relativity and are visually indistinguishable across the sampled couplings, consistent with earlier EMD simulations. For the highly charged binaries with equal-magnitude opposite charges, however, the dominant gravitational strain exhibits visible differences between the EMD cases with $a\neq0$ and the charged Einstein-Maxwell reference at $a=0$. At $a=1$, the coordinate-time interval from the same separation to the waveform-based merger is approximately $62\%$ shorter than for the neutral binary. In this high-charge sequence at fixed input charges, increasing $a$ strengthens the scalar dressing while leaving the individual dilaton-weighted horizon charges nearly unchanged. Within the same sequence, increasing $a$ across the sampled values decreases the dipolar electromagnetic-flux peak, increases the scalar-flux peak, and modestly lengthens the merger interval. The sampled like-charged binaries have corresponding merger intervals approximately $15\%$-$20\%$ longer than the neutral baseline and emit predominantly quadrupolar electromagnetic radiation. At $a=1$ and $a=\sqrt{3}$, the like-charged mergers leave charged remnants with scalar fields consistent with secondary dilaton hair. The opposite-charge remnants instead approach neutral black holes without stationary scalar hair.

entry.title: Robust paths to primordial $B$ modes in the presence of polarised point source contamination
entry.summary: A detection of primordial $B$ modes in the Cosmic Microwave Background (CMB) polarisation relies on a robust control and removal of contamination from astrophysical polarised foreground emission. We examine how much polarised extragalactic point sources may contaminate the cosmological signal in ground-based CMB experiments, propagating their impact through component separation to the final parameter constraints. We discuss masking and modelling strategies to ensure that the resulting constraints remain both accurate and precise under this source of contamination. We produce synthetic data containing polarised emission from extragalactic radio sources (ERSs) and dusty star-forming galaxies (DSFGs) following state-of-the-art models for both samples. We find that, while the DSFG contribution is likely too small to cause any significant bias to the cosmological or foreground parameters, the ERS contribution instead, if left unmasked, leads to a bias in the parameters describing the Galactic synchrotron and lensing $B$-mode components. For experiments targeting noise levels of order $σ_P\simeq 1\,μK\,{\rm arcmin}$, we find that masking all ERSs with fluxes above $\sim$0.1 Jy, coupled with a relatively simple model to marginalise over residual point-source contamination, achieves a suitable balance that allows for the robust recovery of unbiased cosmological and foreground parameters at a negligible cost in parameter uncertainties.

entry.title: Quantum Constrained Hamiltonian Descent
entry.summary: We propose Quantum Constrained Hamiltonian Descent (QCHD), a continuous-time quantum framework for optimization under smooth equality constraints. The unconstrained counterpart, Quantum Hamiltonian Descent (QHD), minimizes a cost function by simulating the Schrödinger dynamics of a particle in the potential given by the cost function. Applying Dirac's formalism to the classical dynamics with constraints, we construct an intrinsic quantum Hamiltonian with a Laplace--Beltrami operator on the constraint manifold in a kinetic term. Its evolution preserves the constraints exactly without penalty terms and is expected to solve quantum-dynamically the constrained optimization problem. We analyze its relation to Quantum Hamiltonian Descent supplemented by a strong penalty term. For a squared-distance penalty, the effective tangential dynamics acquires an extrinsic-curvature potential and, in nontrivial normal-rotation sectors, a coupling to the normal-bundle connection. These embedding-dependent terms remain in the strong-penalty limit, generally yielding quantum dynamics different from QCHD. Numerical comparisons for circular, elliptical, and two simultaneous constraints show faster optimization and improved concentration near global minima for the initial states and finite penalty strengths considered.

entry.title: Integral representations of quantum Rényi divergences on von Neumann algebras
entry.summary: We prove an integral representation of the $α$-$z$ Rényi divergences for normal states on arbitrary von Neumann algebras. Along each ray $z=cα$, the divergence is a positive average of relative entropies evaluated in a canonical family of escort states. For orders $α$ above one, we require the divergence to be finite, whereas for orders below one support inclusion suffices. An explicit boundary correction removes the lower-order support assumption. The proof uses a compatible weighted Haagerup $L^p$ scale and applies outside the data-processing region. For faithful density matrices, we express the derivative of the escort relative entropy with respect to the Rényi order in terms of a nonnegative fluctuation quantity. Differences of order-one derivatives of the divergence give quantum Fisher information and Wigner-Yanase skew information. For faithful bipartite density matrices, we also express optimized conditional $α$-$z$ entropies at orders above one as averages of ordinary conditional entropies. Further applications concern coherent-state divergences in quantum field theory and the optimizing order for the strong converse exponent in hypothesis-testing.

entry.title: A cosmic filament catalog for COSMOS-Web Data Release 1 across 0.5 < z < 3.5
entry.summary: Cosmic filaments represent the environments in which most galaxies form and evolve. However, the spatial distribution of filaments and the link between galaxy properties and their positions relative to filaments remains unclear, particularly at high redshifts. In this work, using the deep-field catalog COSMOS-Web Data Release 1, we construct a filament catalog spanning 0.5 < z < 3.5 that can be directly applied to studies of galaxy evolution and the galaxy--large-scale-structure connection at the peak epoch of galaxy and black hole formation. We developed a new procedure based on the DisPerSE method that fully incorporates the probability distribution functions (PDFs) of galaxy photometric redshifts by generating multiple realizations for each tomographic 2D slice. We then stacked these realizations to construct ``filament probability maps'' (w_ fil maps), from which filaments were subsequently extracted. The filament extraction parameters were optimized using mock catalogs generated from TNG simulations by minimizing the discrepancies between 3D and projected 2D filaments. Applying this procedure to the COSMOS-Web data, we detected 12,523 filaments (comprising 136,210 segments) across 0.5 < z < 3.5 and released a filament catalog, a companion segment catalog, and filament probability maps for each slice. Validation against astrophysical properties shows a strong agreement between the extracted filaments and those in the simulations, supporting the robustness of the filament extraction. These data products provide a robust foundation for investigating galaxy--environment coevolution at cosmic noon and beyond.

entry.title: Identifying galactic binary systems of neutron stars and black holes with LISA
entry.summary: The Laser Interferometer Space Antenna (LISA) will detect $\sim 100$ galactic binary systems comprised of black holes and neutron stars. Distinguishing these binaries from the $\sim 10^4$ double white dwarfs detectable by LISA will be challenging. In the absence of any other information, the inferred component masses can be used to classify the nature of these objects. However, short-period galactic binaries $\sim 10^7$--$10^3\,\mathrm{yr}$ from coalescence produce a quasi-monochromatic signal which carries little information about their masses. We generate synthetic LISA data sets containing gravitational waves from Galactic binary black holes, binary neutron stars and black hole-neutron stars drawn from an astrophysically realistic population produced through the isolated binary evolution channel. We use a Bayesian inference pipeline to explore the accuracy with which the component masses can be measured. LISA will be able to infer component masses for $\approx 10\% - 50\%$ of the detected systems by measuring the orbital eccentricity, periapse precession frequency, and gravitational-wave induced frequency derivative. Typical fractional mass errors are $\approx 1\%$--$100\%$ (depending on the specific value of the source parameters) enabling the classification of the constituent objects as black holes or neutron stars. For these binaries, LISA will also be able to determine their 3-dimensional position in the Milky Way. LISA detections of these double compact objects will provide new insights to their astrophysical formation processes, the Galactic population, and the Milky Way's star formation history. However, for a significant fraction of the LISA-detected binaries the nature of their constituent objects may remain unclear.

entry.title: Many-body localization
entry.summary: We present an introductory review of nonergodic dynamics in interacting many-body quantum systems, focusing on the phenomenon of many-body localization (MBL). We describe aspects of MBL and summarize the evidence for a crossover from the ergodic to the MBL regime in finite systems, using the paradigmatic XXZ model as an example. We then broaden the scope to other models to illustrate the generality of the phenomenon. We briefly touch on the largely unexplored relation between MBL and quantum computing.

entry.title: Exploring the connection between Fast Radio Bursts and binary neutron star mergers
entry.summary: Fast Radio Bursts (FRBs) are highly energetic radio sources whose duration is of the order of milliseconds. The physical origin of these sources is still unknown. Many models suggest magnetars as possible progenitors of FRBs, and this is supported by the association between FRBs and the Galactic magnetar SGR 1935+2154; other proposed progenitors include binary neutron star (BNS) mergers, that are themselves linked to magnetar formation. In this work we investigate the possible connection between FRBs and BNS mergers, including magnetars that might be produced in such events, by comparing the detection rates inferred from synthetic BNS and associated FRB populations with the rates observed by CHIME. We produce a synthetic catalog of BNS mergers by combining recent theoretically predicted BNS merger rate as a function of redshift and the neutron star mass distribution inferred from measurements of Galactic BNSs. Using this catalog we predict the number of BNS systems ending as magnetars (stable or supramassive neutron star) or black holes (formed promptly or after the collapse of a hypermassive neutron star) for different equations of state. We then simulate for each BNS (and therefore for each magnetar remnant) an associated FRB and estimate how many of them can be potentially detected by CHIME. We find that the rate of BNS mergers and the rate of magnetars produced after BNS represents a non-negligible fraction of the FRBs detected by CHIME, both repeating and non-repeating. Although additional formation channels need to be considered to account for the entire population of FRBs, the existence of a fraction of FRBs that might genuinely be associated to BNS mergers has profound implications in the context of multi- messenger astronomy, supporting the systematic searches of coincident detections of FRBs and GWs from a BNS merger with current and future facilities.

entry.title: Interaction-enhanced antiferromagnetic correlations in a Kondo ladder with a gapped band structure
entry.summary: We investigate magnetic correlations in the two-leg Kondo-Hubbard ladder using the density-matrix renormalization group method. We focus on a parameter regime in which the noninteracting electronic system has a narrow indirect band gap. In this regime, there is no Fermi surface, and the conventional Fermi-surface-based Ruderman-Kittel-Kasuya-Yosida picture is not directly applicable; magnetic correlations between localized spins become weaker as the noninteracting band gap increases. We find that a moderate on-site Coulomb interaction enhances the antiferromagnetic correlations between localized spins. This enhancement, which is also seen in the staggered magnetization induced by a pinning field at the edges, occurs for both ferromagnetic and antiferromagnetic Kondo couplings. Our results show that electron-electron interactions can enhance magnetic correlations between localized spins even when the underlying noninteracting electronic structure is gapped, suggesting an interaction-driven route to magnetic instabilities in narrow-gap Kondo-lattice systems.

entry.title: Efficient Eccentric and Quasicircular Effective-One-Body Waveforms via Near-Identity Averaging Transformations
entry.summary: Next-generation gravitational-wave detectors, such as LISA, the Einstein Telescope, and Cosmic Explorer, will require accurate and efficient models of long-lived, eccentric black-hole binary signals. In previous work, we reduced the cost of evolving nonspinning eccentric effective-one-body dynamics by recasting the equations of motion in terms of osculating orbital elements and applying near-identity averaging transformations to remove the fast orbital-timescale structure during the inspiral. However, the parametrization in terms of the eccentricity and relativistic anomaly becomes singular in the circular-orbit limit, excluding quasicircular binaries and the late stages of eccentric inspirals. Moreover, the cost of generating the waveform from the averaged dynamics limited the overall speed-up to a factor of $1.5-8$. In this work, we replace the eccentricity and relativistic anomaly by the Cartesian components of the eccentricity vector, in which the averaged equations are regular for all eccentricities $0 \leq e < 1$. We also decompose the waveform modes into radial harmonics whose coefficients are tabulated as functions of the averaged variables, so that the waveform is assembled directly on the output time grid at a fixed cost per sample. We validate the method against the full effective-one-body evolution across the parameter space of binaries observable by ground-based detectors, now including circular orbits. At second postadiabatic order, the waveforms reach median mismatches of $\sim 10^{-8}$ with a maximum of $1.1 \times 10^{-5}$, while achieving speed-ups of $3-100 \times$ on a single core or up to $300 \times$ on eight cores against the serial EOB waveform. Given the speed-ups demonstrated here, we plan to apply these techniques to state-of-the-art SEOBNR models in future work.

entry.title: Quasinormal modes of Type I perturbations of dilaton-Euler-Heisenberg black holes
entry.summary: We study the type I quasinormal modes (QNMs) of magnetically charged dilaton--Euler--Heisenberg (dEH) black holes, where axial gravitational and polar electromagnetic perturbations are coupled. Direct integration and Chebyshev pseudospectral methods give consistent QNM frequencies for the fundamental branches continued from Schwarzschild at $\ell=1,2,3$. Varying $α$ at fixed $ζ=α-β$ changes the spectrum on the same background. The damping response depends on charge and multipole and can have opposite signs for the two coupled branches. For $ζ<0$, dipole damping decreases with charge toward horizon merger. For $ζ>0$, the Type I charge range extends beyond the complementary polarization's local angular-gradient bound. All tracked modes remain damped in the nonextremal ranges, supporting the stability of these branches.

entry.title: The often overlooked role of sound in liquid thermal transport
entry.summary: Formulated a hundred years ago, the Bridgman formula for thermal conductivity of liquids postulates a proportionality between sound velocity and thermal conductivity. This designates phonons as heat carriers in a liquid. Its empirical success has been under-appreciated and its conceptual implications overlooked. It is not mentioned in well-known condensed-matter textbook. Here, we review its origin, its links to hydrodynamic Euler equations and to the fundamental paradox surrounding the parabolic heat equation and its fate across the quantum-classical crossover.

entry.title: Saxion Decay and Dark Radiation in the KSVZ Axion Model
entry.summary: We calculate the relativistic axion energy density produced by the decay of a curvature-displaced Peccei--Quinn condensate in a quartic KSVZ model. We follow the radial PQ field (the saxion) as it relaxes from its inflationary minimum and determine the surviving condensate abundance from the adiabatic action of its oscillations. We then evolve the condensate through its decay into axions and visible particles to calculate the resulting dark-radiation contribution, expressed as $ΔN_{\rm eff}$. With one heavy coloured KSVZ fermion and no additional portal interactions included, the axion channel dominates the two tree-level decay modes. Two reference histories yield $ΔN_{\rm eff}\simeq0.033$ and $0.12$, with maximum saxion energy fractions below $1\%$ and $4\%$, respectively. At fixed quartic coupling, increasing the duration of curvature release reduces the predicted axion radiation density relative to visible radiation by a factor of approximately $28$ while preserving the primordial isocurvature amplitude.

entry.title: Cosmological Inference with Gravitational-Wave Dark Sirens and 21-cm Intensity Mapping: Forecasts for LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA with MeerKAT and SKAO
entry.summary: Gravitational waves (GWs) and 21-cm intensity mapping (IM) are emerging as complementary cosmological probes: GWs provide direct luminosity-distance measurements, while neutral-hydrogen (HI) IM traces the matter distribution in redshift space. Their synergy offers a promising avenue for precise measurements of the Hubble constant. Within a standard-siren framework, we perform a joint cosmological and population analysis using $\mathcal{O}(150)$ mock GW detections with SNR > 12, as projected for one year of observations at LVK O5 sensitivity. We combine these with mock HI intensity maps from MeerKLASS and SKA-Mid, and study how observational limitations in both the GW and IM data affect the $H_0$ constraints. We find that uncertainty in GW parameter measurements is a dominant limitation on the cosmological constraints. Neglecting this uncertainty, the inclusion of HI information enables sub-percent constraints on $H_0$. We also find that observational effects in the HI surveys weaken the constraints, although they remain tighter than those obtained without HI information (spectral sirens). Despite accounting for HI IM observational limitations, including HI information reduces the $H_0$ uncertainty relative to the spectral-siren results by 61% for MeerKLASS and 53% for SKA-Mid. Because our results are based on a single realisation, they should be interpreted in light of possible realisation-to-realisation variability. Beam convolution most severely weakens the constraints. Instrumental noise can induce multimodality in the posterior, potentially biasing the inferred parameters. The results are sensitive to foreground under-cleaning and over-cleaning. Partial sky coverage has a relatively small impact. In the most realistic scenario, which accounts for both GW and HI IM limitations, we obtain $H_0$ precision estimates of 10% and 15% for MeerKLASS and SKA-Mid, respectively.

entry.title: Hamiltonian formulation of Carrollian Maxwell theory in Deformed Light-cone Kaluza-Klein-like Null reduction
entry.summary: We construct magnetic and electric Carrollian Maxwell theories by performing Kaluza--Klein-like null reduction of a complex Maxwell field in a Bargmann deformed light-cone background with manifest gauge symmetry. The procedure preserves the original first-class U(1) Gauss constraint in the standard Carrollian Maxwell theories and deformed Carrollian Maxwell theories with a decoupled electric/magnetic scalar $A_-$. We give the scaling of the parent gauge parameter and show that the U(1) symmetry is inherited from the parent theory and not introduced after the limit. We emphasize that $A_-$ can be rendered non-dynamical by imposing additional ad hoc constraints. Since $A_-$ is invariant under the original U(1) symmetry, removing it is a constraint and not a gauge choice, but the resulting theory is the same as the one reached by imposing the light-cone gauge $A_- = 0$ prior to the KK-like null reduction. For an electric pseudo-coupled theory without gauge symmetry, after imposing the ad hoc constraints the theory becomes the standard electric Maxwell theory together with a decoupled zero-energy scalar $A_-$. Furthermore, our work provides an explicit example of the correct application of this approach, thereby broadening the scope of its applicability to gauge theories.
entry.arxiv:comment: 13 pages, 2 figures, accepted version for PRD

entry.title: Examining the Anomalous Nature of Chiral Effects in Thermodynamics
entry.summary: Quantum anomalies give rise to novel transport phenomena, including the generation of a current in a relativistic fluid due to the presence of magnetic field or vorticity. We present an exclusive and direct computation of the chiral anomaly in the adiabatic regime within the path integral for a massless fermion on a generic electromagnetic and curved background, including local temperature and chemical potential. We identify new quantum-thermodynamical contributions to the breaking of axial symmetry which induce the Chiral Separation and Vortical Effects.

entry.title: Assessing the consistency of the CPL dark-energy model with cosmological data: Simulation-calibrated neural posterior disagreement
entry.summary: Recent DESI observations hint at a preference for dynamical dark energy with an equation of state that crosses the phantom divide within the Chevallier-Polarski-Linder (CPL) parameterization. In this work, we assess the consistency of the CPL parameterization with current cosmological observations. We develop a model check based on the disagreement between posteriors inferred by neural posterior estimation and flow-matching posterior estimation. Both estimators are trained on the same CPL simulations, and their posterior disagreement is calibrated using independent simulations to obtain a global $p$-value. Controlled simulations assess the reliability of the calibrated \(p\)-values and show how detection sensitivity depends on the form of departure from the assumed model. Applying the test to the compressed CMB+DESI+DESY5 data vector yields $p_{\rm global}=0.524$, indicating that the current observations are consistent with the CPL model. The method has a median evaluation time of only $0.53\,{\rm s}$, enabling efficient assessments of cosmological model adequacy. This framework enables efficient tests of dark-energy models, providing a firmer basis for investigating the physical origin of cosmic acceleration.

entry.title: The subcritical accelerating Schwarzschild-Bertotti-Robinson family
entry.summary: We identify the general finite-$\ell$ neutral Alekseev--Astorino Schwarzschild--Bertotti--Robinson family with the subcritical branch of the independently obtained accelerating Schwarzschild--Bertotti--Robinson solution. The exact scale-free dictionary is \begin{equation*} B^2M^2=\frac{m^2}{b^2+\ell^2},\qquad AM=\frac{m\ell}{b^2+\ell^2},\qquad \frac{A}{B}=\frac{\ell}{\sqrt{b^2+\ell^2}}, \end{equation*} up to the north--south orientation convention. Thus finite real $\ell$ covers precisely the acceleration interval $|A|<|B|$: for $\ell\ne0$ the corresponding OP acceleration parameter is nonzero and the two axial openings are unequal, although no acceleration horizon is present. We establish the identification by canonical Weyl-rod matching and horizon-shape comparison, an independent conicity check, and an exact off-horizon reconstruction of the metric and Maxwell field. The centered limit $\ell=0$ is the nonaccelerating Schwarzschild--BR solution, whereas $|\ell|\to\infty$ approaches the critical boundary $|A/B|=1$ from below. The Astorino parameter $\ell$ therefore parametrizes subcritical acceleration rather than an additional independent neutral black-hole degree of freedom.

entry.title: Parameter Constraints on $f(R^{1+ε},T_{μν}T^{μν})$ Gravity from Exotic Compact Objects
entry.summary: According to General Relativity (GR), gravity is described as the curvature of spacetime caused by mass and energy. Although GR has been highly successful in describing gravitational phenomena, exotic compact objects with high mass and strong gravitational fields, as well as low-mass objects, have motivated the study of modified theories of gravity. One of the modified gravity frameworks is $f(R,T^2) = R^{1 + ε} + ακ^2 T_{μν} T^{μν}$, which provides an extension of GR by introducing modifications to both the geometric and matter sectors. In this study, we investigate the mass-radius structure, physical viability, and stability of quark stars in $f(R,T^2)$ gravity using the MIT Bag Model equation of state. We compare results from the exact $f(R,T^2)$ model, its first-order Taylor expansion, and GR. The values of the gravity parameter $ε$ and $α$ are constrained by evaluating the ability of the model to reproduce the observed mass-radius configurations of compact objects, including HESS J1731-347 with a mass of $M = 0.77_{-0.17}^{+0.20} \, M_{\odot}$ and a radius of $R = 10.4_{-0.78}^{+0.86}$ km, GW190814 with a mass of $M = 2.6 \, M_{\odot}$, PSR J1614-2230, with a mass of $M = 1.928 \pm 0.017 \, M_{\odot}$ and a radius of $R > 10$ km, and PSR J0437-4715, with a mass of $M = 1.418 \pm 0.037 \, M_{\odot}$ and a radius of $R = 11.36_{-0.63}^{+0.95}$ km. We assess the physical viability and stability of the stellar configurations using the energy conditions (strong, weak, null, and dominant) and the speed of sound. Overall, the $f(R,T^2)$ gravity model can accommodate quark star configurations and reproduce the observed properties of massive compact objects, particularly those associated with GW190814 and the lightest compact object observed, HESS J1731-347, respectively.

entry.title: Small black hole in de Sitter as an observer
entry.summary: We study the Euclidean path integral around magnetically charged lukewarm black holes in four-dimensional de Sitter space. We numerically determine the full one-loop spectrum of coupled graviton and photon fluctuations and find that the phase of the partition function agrees with that of pure gravity in empty de Sitter plus a worldline observer. In the small-mass limit, certain localized eigenmodes can be effectively viewed as describing the observer's motion and have the expected eigenvalues, allowing us to reconstruct the worldline action. We further identify these modes with translational zero modes of an extremal charged black hole in asymptotically flat spacetime, lifted by de Sitter curvature.

entry.title: Brane flows
entry.summary: Based on effective D-brane actions, we present a generalisation of the Ricci flow that includes the flow of a theory with a $n$-form field strength for $n\geq 0$. This is a generalisation of both the Ricci flows and the generalised Ricci flows. Following Perelman, we show that flows that keep a suitable field-dependent volume fixed are monotonic. We also show that all steady brane flow solitons are gradient solitons and use this to demonstrate that on some occasions this implies the existence of a Killing vector field that leaves all the other fields invariant. Particular cases of gradient solitons are NS5 and D5 branes, and the volume which is kept fixed in these cases is the T-duality invariant volume (NS5 brane) or its S-dual (D5 brane). We also generalise the above analysis to gravitational actions coupled to form gauge potentials that also exhibit a Chern-Simons type term. We find an alteration is required in the adaptation of Perelman's modification to this case, which yields a new functional that also exhibits a Chern-Simons term. Under suitable assumptions, we proceed to prove the monotonicity of the flow and that all steady flow solitons are gradient solitons. We also explore the consequences of the last statement on the geometry of solitons.

entry.title: From Fredholm Determinants to AdS/CFT Observables: A Universal Strong-Coupling Framework
entry.summary: We investigate the trans-series structure of the cusp anomalous dimension of $\mathcal{N}=4$ supersymmetric Yang-Mills theory and the dynamically generated mass gap of the $\mathrm{O}(6)$ sigma model at strong 't Hooft coupling. We consider the one-parameter deformation of the cusp anomalous dimension, known as the tilted cusp, and review its strong-coupling expansion obtained through its representation in terms of Fredholm determinants with a matrix Bessel kernel. The advantage of this deformation is that the non-perturbative scales separate naturally, revealing structures that remain hidden in the physical limit. Motivated by this observation, we introduce the tilted mass gap, which reduces to the physical $\mathrm{O}(6)$ mass gap at a special value of the deformation parameter and exhibits a deep connection with the tilted cusp. This formulation allows us to determine the complete strong-coupling trans-series and resurgence structure of the $\mathrm{O}(6)$ mass gap, while extending and proving conjectured relations between successive non-perturbative corrections. Building on the underlying Fredholm determinant representation, we construct an Alien calculus that generates all non-perturbative sectors of these AdS/CFT observables directly from their perturbative expansions. Finally, we derive an exact all-orders relation between the strong-coupling trans-series of the $\mathrm{O}(6)$ mass gap and the cusp anomalous dimension of planar $\mathcal{N}=4$ supersymmetric Yang-Mills theory.

entry.title: A large size of the pion-like excitations in the stringy fluid above $T_{ch}$ is model independent and required by current algebra
entry.summary: Multiple lattice evidences support the existence of a confining but chirally symmetric stringy fluid regime of QCD above the chiral symmetry restoration temperature at T_{ch} ~ 155 MeV. This regime is characterized by an approximate chiral spin symmetry and its extensions which means that the propagating excitations represent the chirally symmetric quarks connected into color singlets by the chromoelectric string. Clear π,π' peaks above T_{ch} were extracted on the lattice from the spatial and temporal correlators, which become broader with temperature and disappear roughly at $3T_{ch}$. The meson-like excitations above T_{ch} were studied within the manifestly confining and chirally symmetric model. It has been demonstrated that the chiral symmetry restoration in the confining regime happens because of Pauli blocking of the levels, required for the existence of the quark condensate, by the thermal quark excitation. The same Pauli blocking leads to a huge swelling of the low-spin mesons above T_{ch} which become infinitely large in the chiral limit. This property should be crucial for the explanation of the high collectivity and a very small mean-free path of the constituents above $T_{ch}$ seen experimentally. Here we demonstrate that the swelling of pions above T_{ch} is a model-independent effect required by current algebra.

entry.title: Chiral Transport in Metric-Affine Geometries
entry.summary: Anomalous transport in equilibrium fermionic fluids chirally coupled to background Weyl-type nonmetricity is studied. A formal descent analysis is carried out in which the dependence of the anomaly polynomial on the nonmetricity tensor is encoded in a Weyl invariant four-form. The constitutive relation of the axial-vector current is evaluated from the equilibrium partition function obtained using transgression techniques, showing the existence of nonmetricity-mediated chiral separation effects driven by the fluid's vorticity and the Weyl magnetic field. A second nonminimal coupling of fermionic matter to metric-affine geometries proposed in the literature is also discussed.

entry.title: A Casimir turning point as the beginning of a small flat universe
entry.summary: We study a flat three-torus universe whose contraction is turned around by the negative Casimir energy of Standard Model fields. The trace anomaly forbids conformal matter alone to turn an anisotropic universe around, so matter with $w<1/3$, most cheaply a positive potential, must supply the negative trace; with antiperiodic fermions the Standard Model supplies the negative energy, and the universe turns at an edge of 722 reduced Planck lengths. The turning point can hold only about five quanta of the lowest modes, whereas a reheating coupling in a time-symmetric past would produce radiation exceeding the Casimir energy by at least $10^{94}$, so we read the turn as a beginning rather than a bounce. Negative Casimir energy cannot hold the shape of the torus: its shape state can be real at most once, and for a real Gaussian state survival of the shape on both branches with $90\%$ probability requires that moment to lie within $0.35$ Hubble times of the turn. The natural state, real at the turn, freezes the torus into a nearly rectangular box whose sides typically differ by $16$--$18\%$. The microwave background can read this fossil only if the shortest cycle lies between $0.985$ and about $1.04$ last-scattering diameters. At the turn the Higgs quartic coupling is negative, yet zero-point fluctuations of the gauge zero modes keep the Higgs zero mode near the origin with probability above one half for a top-quark pole mass below $172.96$ GeV, given a curvature coupling $ξ_H\gtrsim0.08$; a pole mass above $173.7$ GeV, within reach of FCC-ee, would exclude this beginning.

entry.title: Perfect Born Sampling of Symmetric Thermal Tensor Network States
entry.summary: Accurate calculations of correlated fermions at low temperatures constitute a major challenge in quantum many-body physics, most notably in the studies of high-$T_c$ superconductivity and ultracold atom optical lattices. Stochastic sampling of tensor-network states offers a promising route to tackle this problem; however, existing schemes have long faced a fundamental dilemma---sampling efficiency and symmetry acceleration \textit{cannot} be achieved simultaneously. Here we propose a perfect Born sampling approach for thermal tensor networks, which performs importance sampling directly from the purified density matrix via the Born rule and incorporates Abelian and non-Abelian symmetries by sampling symmetry quantum numbers. We benchmark the method, realized as both stochastic matrix product states (stoMPS) and stochastic projected entangled pair states (stoPEPS), on large-scale quantum lattice models. Using stoMPS, we accurately simulate the square-lattice Hubbard model on cylinders up to width $W=10$, and study the triangular-lattice Hubbard model down to $T/t = 1/64$. We reveal scalar chiral order at half filling and kinetic ferromagnetism upon electron doping, with the latter directly compared to ultracold atom experiments. We further extend the stoMPS method to compute finite-temperature quantum dynamics, as demonstrated by the optical conductivity of the Hubbard model. We showcase the generalization of stoPEPS on up to $20\times20$ square-lattice quantum Ising model, where accurate results are obtained near its quantum critical point. Our method combines high sampling efficiency with full symmetry acceleration. The resulting state-of-the-art framework captures both equilibrium and dynamical properties down to ultralow temperatures, thereby providing a powerful theoretical tool for correlated quantum systems, particularly fermion Hubbard quantum gas microscopy.

entry.title: Construction and phenomenological analysis of dynamical Inverse seesaw neutrino mixing model
entry.summary: In this manuscript, a dynamical inverse seesaw neutrino ISS(3+1+1+1) mixing model based on the gauge symmetry $U(1)_{B-L}$ extended by the flavor symmetry $A_{4}\times Z_{2}$ has been constructed. ISS(3+1+1+1) represents three generations of right-handed neutrinos and an extra three generation of singlets sterile neutrinos, wherein the right-handed neutrinos are triplets under $A_4$ symmetry. Furthermore, the five scalar flavon fields are considered in the model, which reproduce neutrino oscillation data within the NuFIT 6.0 experimental range with statistical $\text{|pull|}=0.01 σ$. The neutrino mass hierarchy is obtained by minimizing the dynamical $A_4\times Z_2$ scalar flavon $φ_v$ potential. The effective neutrino mass parameter $m_{ββ}$ for the neutrinoless double beta decay $0vββ$ has been charecterised in the manuscript. The effective neutrino mass parameter spans a finite region in the parameter space rather then being confined to a single point and it is constrained by the KamLAND-Zen excluded band. The model successfully explains active-sterile neutrino mixing and non-unitarity of the PMNS matrix is consistent with the cosmological upper bound. The minimum value of the sum of the active neutrinos' mass turns out to be $m_{i}\approx 62\ \ (99.4)\ \text{meV}$ for Normal ordering (Inverted ordering), which lies within the range of both Planck 2018 loose cosmological limit $\sum m_{i}<120\ \text{meV}$ and tighter limit $\sum m_{i}<72\ \text{meV}$ of DESI-2024. Our model immensely favours normal ordering, in agreement with the tighter constraints reported by DESI-2024.

entry.title: Weak Radio and Bright Early Optical Emission in EP260321a: A Comparative Study with XRO 080109 Reveals the Role of Circumstellar Material Mass
entry.summary: Shock breakout (SBO) occurs when a radiation-mediated shock wave, formed during a core-collapse supernova (SN) explosion, breaks out from the stellar surface of the progenitor or from the circumstellar material (CSM), if the CSM is optically thick. The X-ray outburst XRO 080109, associated with a Type Ib/c SN 2008D, has been suggested to be an SBO event from a regular supernova. The recent detection of EP260321a, associated with a broad-lined Type Ic SN 2026gzf, by the Einstein Probe adds a new SBO event. However, the two SBO events differ markedly in their spectra, energetics, late-time radio emission and early optical emission within the first day. We show that the non-detections in radio follow-up observations of EP260321a imply a shock velocity $\lesssim0.1c$, whereas the radio data of XRO 080109 suggest a shock velocity of $\simeq0.2c$. These velocities are consistent with those inferred from the properties of the X-ray outbursts and explain the difference in their X-ray spectra. The X-ray energy and duration of EP260321a indicate that the shock breaks out from the CSM at a radius of $\sim2\times10^{13}\ {\rm cm}$. Its bright optical emission at $t\lesssim1\ {\rm d}$ can be explained by cooling emission from a dense, extended CSM shell heated by the radiation-mediated shock, requiring a total CSM mass of $\sim0.06M_\odot$, substantially larger than that inferred for XRO 080109. Finally, the lower shock velocity and larger CSM mass can be unified in a picture in which a more massive CSM decelerates the radiation-mediated shock more significantly before it breaks out.

entry.title: Five-loop static two-body potential in massless scalar-tensor gravity
entry.summary: We compute the static contribution to the conservative two-body potential in massless scalar-tensor theories through fifth post-Newtonian (5PN) order, with the strong-field scalar responses of the compact objects encoded in scalar-dependent masses. Within post-Newtonian effective field theory (EFT), evaluating the 1PN-5PN static terms requires one- through five-loop massless two-point Feynman integrals. Although the additional scalar modifies both source couplings and integrand numerators, the required scalar master topologies remain those of the corresponding static problem in general relativity. Moreover, independent reflection symmetries of the two static scalar sectors extend the odd-PN factorization mechanism to the present theory, so that no genuinely new five-loop master integrals are required. Our results reproduce the known static interaction through 2PN, provide an independent EFT determination at 3PN, and extend the explicit potential to 4PN and 5PN. We verify the general-relativity limit and body-exchange symmetry; regulator poles and residual transcendental terms cancel in the complete result, leaving rational coefficients. These high-precision results provide ingredients for increasingly precise gravitational-wave tests of gravity beyond general relativity.

entry.title: Search for Ultra-Relativistic Magnetic Monopoles with LHAASO-KM2A
entry.summary: Ultra-relativistic magnetic monopoles traversing the atmosphere are expected to initiate extensive air showers characterized by a muon deficit and a compact lateral profile. Using 1438.81 live days of data from the LHAASO-KM2A array, we present a search for these cosmic particles within the Lorentz factor range of $10^5$ to $10^7$. A machine-learning classifier utilizing lateral shower shape observables from the electromagnetic detectors is deployed to separate the signal from the hadronic background. No statistical excess above the background expectation is observed, and upper limits at the 90\% confidence level are established on the isotropic monopole flux. The resulting upper limit is $2.6 \times 10^{-16}\,\mathrm{cm}^{-2}\,\mathrm{s}^{-1}\,\mathrm{sr}^{-1}$ at $γ= 10^5$ and reaches $8.8 \times 10^{-19}\,\mathrm{cm}^{-2}\,\mathrm{s}^{-1}\,\mathrm{sr}^{-1}$ at $γ= 10^7$, which improves upon the astrophysical Parker bound by over three orders of magnitude. This work establishes constraints on the monopole flux within a previously unconstrained velocity window.

entry.title: GPAge: a Global Parameterization based on cosmic Age for some unified early-time and late-time solutions to the Hubble tension
entry.summary: The over $5σ$ Hubble tension continues to motivate modifications of the standard $Λ$-cold-dark-matter ($Λ\rm CDM$) model. The large number of proposed resolutions for the Hubble tension, broadly divided into early- and late-time solutions, motivates phenomenological parametrizations to constrain the viable solution space. Recently, there is a growing interest in unifying early- and late-time solutions. In this work, we extend the original Parametrization based on cosmic Age (PAge) to cover both the early and late Universe. Specifically, we incorporate the radiation-dominated epoch at the background level and complete the perturbation sector within a unified-dark-fluid framework. The resulting parametrization can accurately reproduce target cosmological models at both the background and perturbation levels. Confronting this global PAge with cosmological observations, we find that it improves the best fit relative to $Λ\rm CDM$, but does not raise $H_0$ significantly enough to alleviate the Hubble tension. Our parametrizations indicate that varying the early-time matter-like density, even together with a flexible late-time expansion history, is insufficient to resolve the Hubble tension. These results suggest that resolving the Hubble tension requires pre-recombination physics beyond a simple retuning of the matter-like density.

entry.title: EP J062132.0+623837: A Multi-wavelength Study of a Changing-look Active Galactic Nucleus Discovered by Einstein Probe
entry.summary: EP J062132.0+623837 is a new X-ray source identified in 14-day binned survey data from the Wide-field X-ray Telescope aboard the Einstein Probe (EP). Subsequent X-ray observations with the Follow-up X-ray Telescope (FXT) on board EP localized the source to the central region of the galaxy 2MASX J06213207+6238390 at $z=0.084$. Here, we present a comprehensive analysis of the multi-wavelength data for this object. During the FXT and Swift/XRT follow-up, the source remained X-ray active, with observed luminosities of $(3-9)\times10^{43}$ erg s$^{-1}$, and its X-ray spectra were well described by power-law models with photon indices of $Γ\sim1.5$. The optical spectrum of the host galaxy clearly reveals a broad-line active galactic nucleus (AGN) exhibiting significantly enhanced broad Balmer emission lines compared to an archival spectrum obtained four years earlier, thereby marking a changing-look transition from Type 1.8 to Type 1.5. Furthermore, long-term optical and mid-infrared light curves indicate that the nucleus underwent dramatic brightening around 2010 and has since shown substantial variability. Given the spatial coincidence and multi-wavelength behavior, we identify EP J062132.0+623837 as a changing-look AGN, initially detected by EP and subsequently confirmed to exhibit large-amplitude variability across multiple bands. This case study demonstrates the great potential of wide-field time-domain X-ray surveys for discovering changing-look AGNs, paving a new avenue for their systematic identification as a powerful complement to ongoing optical surveys.

entry.title: Testing Bump in the Cosmological Power Spectrum Using Dwarf Galaxies
entry.summary: We analyze the possibility of using observational data on nearby dwarf galaxies -- their luminosity functions and spatial distributions -- to constrain deviations of the cosmological power spectrum from the standard one. Specifically, we consider a cosmological model with a "bump" in the power spectrum at a wavelength of 1.3~Mpc and a dimensionless amplitude $\mathcal{A}=2.0$. Such a spectrum is motivated by observations of an excess number of galaxies at high redshifts. The bump leads to a noticeable increase in the luminosity function in the range $-13 > M_B > -17$ at $z=0$. Comparison with observations constrains the bump amplitude to $\mathcal{A} < 0.25$ at a 3-sigma significance level for a wavelength of 1.3~Mpc. For wavelengths smaller than 0.8~Mpc, the bump manifests only in the luminosity function of dwarfs with $M_B > -14$.

entry.title: Multi-tracers, multi-surveys: a joint Fisher analysis of DESI+PFS
entry.summary: Marginalizing over 11 effective-field-theory (EFT) nuisance parameters per tracer per redshift bin degrades cosmological precision in one-loop analyses of galaxy power-spectrum multipoles in redshift space. Simulation-based priors (SBP) tighten these parameters but rely on N-body simulations and halo-occupation-distribution (HOD) models. We consider a multi-tracer Fisher analysis as a complementary approach: auto- and cross-power spectra jointly constrain cosmology, galaxy bias and stochasticity through two channels -- within a survey and across overlapping surveys -- combined in a volume-partitioned joint Fisher analysis. We forecast across the $14{,}000\;\mathrm{deg}^2$ Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument (DESI) footprint, including the $\sim\!1{,}200\;\mathrm{deg}^2$ Prime Focus Spectrograph (PFS) overlap at $z\in[0.6,1.6]$ with up to 4 tracers (PFS-ELG, DESI-ELG, DESI-LRG, DESI-QSO). We vary a common $\ln(10^{10}A_s)$, $M_ν$ and $Ω_m$, holding $h$, $ω_b$ and $n_s$ fixed. Adding internal-DESI cross-spectra to DESI auto-spectra reduces the errors on the derived $fσ_8(z=1.1)$, $M_ν$ and $Ω_m$ by 7.1%, 3.5% and 3.8%, respectively, at $k_{\rm max}=0.20\,h\,\mathrm{Mpc}^{-1}$. Adding PFS auto- and cross-spectra to this complete DESI multi-tracer analysis further tightens these errors by 3.8%, 2.6% and 3.2%, respectively, after marginalizing over residual cross-population stochasticity. The clustering likelihood alone constrains the linear and quadratic biases and the shot noise. For these parameters it provides a complementary test of inference using SBP, while the counterterms remain weakly constrained. The framework extends to any number of overlapping spectroscopic surveys.

entry.title: Analytical Time-Domain Waveforms for Black-Hole Scattering in the Self-Force Expansion
entry.summary: We obtain a systematic understanding of the time-domain gravitational waveform of hyperbolic black-hole scattering at first order in the self-force expansion and all orders in the post-Newtonian/post-Minkowskian (PN/PM) expansion. The continuous frequency spectrum of unbound orbits makes the inverse Fourier transform to the time domain diverge order by order; we introduce a dimensional-regularization-inspired prescription that cures this uniformly. We show that the full waveform then follows, at any PM and PN order, from a single family of integrals, generated by the Lauricella function $F_D^{(3)}$, which we calculate using strategies familiar from the study of Feynman integrals. As a proof of principle, we use this understanding to compute the quadrupolar 1SF waveform through relative 10PM-20PN, that is to order ${\cal O}(G^{10} v^{42})$, the full 1SF waveform to 10PM-10PN, as well as the asymptotic fluxes and the dissipative scattering angle at the corresponding accuracy.

entry.title: Quasinormal modes, complex null geodesics and singularity resolution in regular AdS black holes
entry.summary: The black hole singularity is hidden behind its horizon, and it is difficult to determine whether it is resolved by quantum gravity or stringy effects. For an AdS-Schwarzschild black hole, it is known that the two-point function of the dual conformal field theory has a singularity associated with a null geodesic that bounces off the black hole singularity. In this paper, we investigate how the resolution of the black hole singularity is encoded in the dual conformal field theory by considering regular AdS black holes as regularized geometries. Using WKB analysis, we compute the quasinormal modes of regular AdS black holes and read off the dual two-point functions from the modes. We find that the singularity corresponding to the bouncing null geodesic for singular black holes is replaced by a smooth bump associated with a complex, rather than real, null geodesic. The location of the complex geodesic singularity is supported by analyzing the structure of the operator product expansion for the two-point function. Our results provide a holographic signature of black hole singularity resolution and clarify how information about the regular interior is encoded in boundary correlation functions.

entry.title: Slave-boson Formalism for Superconducting Pairing at Strong Coupling
entry.summary: We study the emergence of superconductivity in the one-band Hubbard model using the spin-rotation-invariant Kotliar-Ruckenstein slave-boson (SB) approach. Motivated by its intrinsically renormalized mean-field ground state, we construct an effective pairing vertex from dynamical fluctuations about the saddle point. Solving the anisotropic, frequency-dependent gap equation on the square lattice, we map the pairing instabilities across doping, interaction, temperature and real-frequency gap structure that qualitatively match experimental cuprate observations. This framework merges strong-correlation SB-type renormalizations with RPA-type pairing transparency, providing a scalable route to modeling multi-orbital superconductivity at strong coupling.

entry.title: Photon spheres in dynamical spacetimes
entry.summary: The characterization of the photon region -- i.e. the region of space-time filled with unstable bound null geodesics -- is critical to understand the behavior of radiation near a compact-enough object, such as black holes. However, its study has been typically focused on stationary space-times that leave outside interesting theoretical and phenomenological scenarios such as collapsing, accreting, or evaporating black holes, besides time-dependent configurations such as those found in some boson star models. In this work, we present a novel covariant approach to describe radiation in dynamical spherical space-times. This allows a general description of photon surfaces and their dynamics in non-static space-times, recovering well known expressions in the static limit and clarifying their meanings. Furthermore, we illustrate our results via several examples of dynamical scenarios in stellar collapse and accreting/evaporating models, and discuss the open caveats regarding such scenarios.

entry.title: Relativistic Dynamical Evolution of Kilonova Spectral Emission
entry.summary: We develop a relativistic dynamical model for the thermal evolution of expanding kilonova ejecta, in which the effective temperature is determined by the ejecta mass, opacity, velocity, and radioactive heating rate. The resulting thermal evolution follows a broken power law as the ejecta transition from the optically thick to the optically thin regime. We incorporate this thermal history into a relativistic spectral calculation that accounts for the equal-arrival-time surface geometry and Doppler boosting, enabling us to model the observed kilonova spectrum and constrain the underlying ejecta properties. We investigate the effects of the model parameters and relativistic corrections on the observed temperature and spectral shape, and find that light-travel-time delays and Doppler shifts can produce significant spectral distortions at high ejecta velocities. We apply the model to the early-time X-shooter spectrum of the kilonova AT2017gfo and infer the ejecta mass, opacity, and velocity through Markov chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) fitting with a Student's $t$ likelihood. We find that relativistic effects become increasingly important for fast ejecta ($v \gtrsim 0.5c$), particularly at large viewing angles, where the observed temperature can differ substantially from the rest-frame effective temperature. These results highlight the importance of incorporating relativistic and equal-arrival-time effects when interpreting early-time kilonova spectra, especially for rapidly expanding ejecta.
